text: Despite the cultural trope depicting emotions as the opposite of rational thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Cognition, what we commonly refer to as thinking. <break time="0.8s" /> Is actually a key building block of emotion. <break time="0.8s" /> How we think about our circumstances. <break time="0.8s" /> Shapes the emotions we experience. <break time="0.8s" /> Then those emotions echo back. <break time="0.8s" /> To influence how we think. <break time="0.8s" /> For instance. <break time="0.8s" /> If you walk into a test. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking you are bad at taking tests. <break time="0.8s" /> Your anxiety will be increased. <break time="0.8s" /> Then you do not feel good. <break time="0.8s" /> About your performance on the test. <break time="0.8s" /> And that becomes evidence. <break time="0.8s" /> For continuing to think that you are bad at test taking. <break time="0.8s" /> In this way. <break time="0.8s" /> There is simply no pulling emotion and cognition apart. <break time="0.8s" /> This bi directionality of cognition and emotion. <break time="0.8s" /> Allows us to adjust difficult emotions. <break time="0.8s" /> By changing the way we think. <break time="0.8s" /> By thinking differently. <break time="0.8s" /> , I get nervous sometimes. <break time="0.8s" /> But I am still a good test taker. <break time="0.8s" /> Or that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation. <break time="0.8s" /> It means I am ready. <break time="0.8s" /> You can work those pathways. <break time="0.8s" /> To your advantage.
